### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A16, A17 and A18 each appear in about 79% of traces, up from about 19% in the earlier window; activities A19, A20 and A21 each appear in about 21% of traces, down from about 82% [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006].
- The outgoing transitions of A15 shifted: in the earlier window about 29% went to A19, 24% to A20 and 28% to A21, with small shares to A16–A18; in the later window about 29% go to A18, 21% to A17 and 28% to A16, with small shares to A19–A21 [DIR001].
- A15 co-occurs with A16, A17 and A18 in about 79% of traces in the later window, up from about 19%; it co-occurs with A19, A20 and A21 in about 21%, down from about 82% [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006].
- Among A16–A18, co-occurrence rose from about 19% to about 79%, with both orders appearing in the later window (e.g., A16 before A17 in 41.5% and A17 before A16 in 37.5% of traces); among A19–A21, co-occurrence fell from about 82% to about 21% [REL007, REL008, REL013, REL022, REL023, REL025].
- A25 now co-occurs with A16–A18 in about 79% of traces (up from 19%) and with A19–A21 in about 21% (down from 82%) [REL012, REL017, REL021, REL024, REL026, REL027].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in the process structure: after activity A15, the process now executes the group A16–A18 instead of the group A19–A21. This is shown directly by the shift in participation of these activities, the redistribution of A15's outgoing transitions, and the corresponding changes in co-occurrence with A25. The order within the new group is not fixed (both orders occur), similar to the earlier group. The large number of qualifying items (34 vs. 0.52 expected by chance) rules out a chance sampling difference. A competing explanation that the earlier group was simply skipped is not supported, because the new group appears in the same position and with the same relationship to A15 and A25.
